name: Carpet & upholstery cleaner

pf.license.need: Usually none for carpet, rug or upholstery cleaning. Where a state's or city's rules ask for a license or a business registration, its form asks for it.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Carpet techs need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: Insured or bonded is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie. A building that asks for proof of insurance gets it from the owner.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Mold removal, water-damage drying and sewage cleanup, and flea or bedbug treatment, are licensed in many states. A carpet cleaner doesn't take them on; the state's form says which license each one needs.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: carpet cleaning at the customer's place, priced by the room or the square foot, with stains noted before work. Rugs can also be dropped off at the plant.
pf.services.unit: A room is up to 250 sq ft; a bigger room counts as 2. The AI asks the rooms and rough sizes before any times, and the price shows with that rule. At the visit the count changes only for what the tech measures, with the customer's yes first.

list.name: Carpet cleaning, 3 rooms
list.price_kind: one price, set by the number of rooms
list.example: $179 for up to 3 rooms; each extra room $55; a hall or walk-in closet $25; stairs $4 a step (the example business's own prices)
list.length: about 30 minutes a room, plus the walk-through before work
list.money: the $89 trip fee held at booking; Rosie texts the bill at DONE

list.name: Carpet by the square foot
list.price_kind: quoted at the visit, after the tech measures (a basement, an open floor or an office)
list.example: only the $89 trip fee is promised; the example: a 600 sq ft basement $165, 20 stairs $80
list.money: the $89 trip fee held; the price OK'd at the visit goes on the bill

list.name: Pet odor treatment, whole home
list.price_kind: quoted from the customer's photos first
list.example: $640 for 5 rooms and the stairs with old pet urine; over Sam's $500 limit, so Sam OKs it
list.length: a long day, often two techs
list.money: the $89 trip fee held; the rest on the bill

list.name: Pet urine treatment (add-on)
list.price_kind: one price, only when the customer asks
list.example: $199 for up to 3 rooms; a UV light finds the spots

list.name: Found at the visit (add-ons)
list.price_kind: quoted before it's done, the customer's yes first
list.example: re-stretching a rippled room $160; rust stain treatment $95; stain protector $20 a room

list.name: Upholstery cleaning (the second kind of work)
list.price_kind: one price per piece, by the fabric tag (W, S, W/S, X)
list.example: loveseat $149, sofa up to 3 seats $189, by the hour $120 (1-hour minimum); a sectional gets a free estimate visit, then a quote

list.name: Area rug cleaning
list.price_kind: one price by size, from photos (pet stains), or at the counter (hand-knotted rugs)
list.example: small rug up to 4 by 6 ft $35, runner $40, doormat $25, fringe cleaning $20, small rug with stain protector $55, large wool rug up to 8 by 10 ft $140, pet stain treatment from photos ($90 in the example), hand-knotted rugs priced at the counter after a $25 inspection
list.where: dropped off at the plant; a rug can also be cleaned at the customer's home ($75), or taken to the plant by the tech
list.money: nothing taken; paid at the counter at pick-up

list.name: Trip fee
list.example: $89: owed only for a late cancel or nobody home, when the owner confirms it; or when a job priced at the visit isn't done; credited to the job

pf.services.capacity: One carpet tech per home job, with the van's truck-mounted unit. A whole-home pet odor job or an empty rental can take two. The plant takes a set number of rugs a day.
pf.services.nobody_home: Only for an empty home, like a rental between tenants, with the owner's or manager's OK and a lockbox. Otherwise an adult is home from the window's start until done.
pf.services.not_offered: Water-damage drying, flood or sewage cleanup, mold removal, flea or bedbug treatment. The rest of the home can still be booked with that part left out.
pf.services.drop_off_slots: Rugs are booked into drop-off slots by the plant's daily rug count, with no rug tech named. A rug goes to a rug tech with the skill once it's in.
pf.services.owner_looks_first: Pet urine and water-stain jobs can go to Sam first: the time stays saved while Sam looks at the photos.

before_times: How many rooms, and about how big is each (any bigger than about 15 by 16 ft)?
Halls, closets or stairs, and how many steps
Any pet stains: which rooms, fresh or old
Any sofa or chair, and what its fabric tag says (W, S, W/S or X)
For a rug at the plant: its size and what it's made of, if known
after_a_time: Heavy furniture in the rooms, like beds, dressers or a piano (they stay put)
Where pets will be during the visit
Rooms to skip, or spots to look at first
Photos of the stains, on the secure page (asked for pet urine or water stains)
secure_page_only: Van parking within 150 feet of the door, and an outdoor water tap
The lockbox or door code for an empty rental
Health reasons behind a product to avoid, like an allergy
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who lives in the home, or the owner, a landlord or a property manager they name (an empty rental).

words: flooding, or water still coming in
water near outlets, cords or the electrical panel; sparks
mold under or behind a carpet
moths or carpet beetles in a rug
what_happens: Flooding, a soaked carpet or sewage: Rosie gives the safety steps (stay out of rooms where water is near outlets; 911 if there are sparks; keep children and pets away from sewage). No booking: a soaked carpet needs a water-damage company within a day or two, before mold starts.
Mold: keep that room closed and don't clean it. Mold needs a licensed pro where the state's rules require one. The other rooms can still be booked.
Fleas or bedbugs: pest control comes first, licensed where the state's rules require it. The cleaning is booked after.
Moths in a rug: the drop-off can move with no fee until they're treated. At the plant, the rug is kept apart from the others.
Found at the visit: a wet pad or mold stops work in that room. Extraction could spread it. A written note goes to the customer, and that room comes off the price.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for flooding, a soaked carpet or sewage. Yes, with that room left out, for mold. After pest control, for fleas or bedbugs.

pf.first_steps.none_needed: Nothing has to happen before a carpet cleaning.
pf.first_steps.photos: A whole-home pet odor job is priced from the customer's photos first. Pet urine and water-stain jobs can go to Sam to look at first.
pf.first_steps.estimate_visit: A sectional sofa or an office gets a free estimate visit first, then a quote.
prep_for_reminder: Pick up small things and toys from the floor
The tech moves chairs, small tables and the sofa; beds, dressers, pianos and electronics stay
Plan on 6 to 8 hours for carpets to dry, 8 to 12 for a sofa
pf.first_steps.rug_at_the_plant: Vacuum the rug, then roll it, don't fold it. A hand-knotted rug gets a color test at the plant before it's washed.

pf.visit.check_in: Someone home: the code at the door, entered by the carpet tech. An empty rental: no code; the tech opens the lockbox, and DONE with photos confirms it.
pf.visit.before_work: Before any work, the tech walks each room with the customer: measures the rooms, checks spots with a UV light, reads any fabric tag, and photographs every stain and worn spot. Stains that may not come all the way out are said out loud and noted.
pf.visit.firm_price: A room price holds unless a room measures bigger. Any change, or extra work found, is quoted and OK'd before it's done. A job priced by the square foot gets its price after measuring, before any work.
pf.visit.how: Hot water extraction with the truck-mounted unit. Furniture goes back on foam blocks so the damp carpet isn't stained.
pf.visit.drop_off: At the plant: the code at the counter when the rug is left. The rug tech measures it and notes stains, worn spots, moth damage and loose fringe before it's washed. Status words IN, DRYING, READY. READY comes with a photo. Pick-up only by the customer or someone they name.
pf.visit.rug_to_the_plant: A tech can take an area rug from the home to the plant, signed out with a photo, and books its return.
pf.visit.proof_done: Before photos of each room and its stains, after photos from the same angles, and a walk-through with the customer before DONE.
pf.visit.breakage: Reported with photos the same day; the owner decides how to make it right.

pf.money.start: At the home: the $89 trip fee held at booking (the example), and Rosie texts the bill at DONE. Some owners save a card and charge it at DONE, take nothing before, or take payment their own way. At the plant: a card saved for the plant's $20 fee (the safe default), the large wool rug's $40 fee held (it runs over 2 hours), or nothing taken, as Sam picks per service; paid at the counter at pick-up.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. Sam can set a deposit or the full price per service, within the state's caps. Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel or nobody home: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89), never more than the job. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee. No trip fee when the customer cancels at the door because the price went up.
pf.money.come_backs: A spot that comes back within 7 days gets a free re-treat. It's a redo, never money from Rosie.
pf.money.tips: Optional. A tip line only if the owner turns it on. How card tips are handled follows the state's rules, from the state form.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes carpet or rug cleaning, from the state form.
pf.money.emergency_prices: In a declared emergency, prices follow the state's limits on price rises, from the state form.

never_in_texts: Health reasons, like an allergy behind a product to avoid
pf.messages.photos: Photos of the home and its stains go only to the customer and the business.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish. The tech's language shows on the job.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the booking's adult.

skills: Carpet cleaning by the room or the square foot
Pet odor and pet urine treatment
Spot and rust stain removal, re-stretching
Rug cleaning at the plant, hand-knotted rugs
pf.staff.crews: One tech per home job. Two for a whole-home pet odor job or an empty rental: a lead, who holds the code and texts DONE, and a helper.
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A stand-in with the same skill is offered to the customer first. No answer by the cutoff: the stand-in keeps the time, and the customer can still move or cancel with no fee.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs quotes over the limit, and pet urine or water-stain jobs he asked to see first. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.

pf.rules.unit_price: A price by the unit says what one unit is (a room up to 250 sq ft) before the yes. The count changes at the visit only for what's measured, with the customer's yes.
pf.rules.add_on_at_home: Extra work sold at the home comes with a written right to cancel and a refund date, where the state's rules give one.
pf.rules.written_contract: Above an amount, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.mold_and_pests: Mold, water damage and pests are left to licensed pros where the state's rules license them. The tech names the kind of pro, never a company.
pf.rules.landlord: A renter's cleaning may be paid by the landlord, who OKs it first.
pf.rules.emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency, from the state form.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, with the before and after photos and the stains noted before work.

matter_most: Stains noted before work: what may not come out is said and photographed first, so a claim later is checked against it.
A room bigger than the rule: counted as 2 only with the customer's yes, before work.
Pet urine found in more rooms at the visit: quoted first; the customer says yes or no.
A wet pad or mold found at the visit: that room stops; a written note; it comes off the price.
A spot comes back within 7 days: a free re-treat.
The price went up at the door and the customer cancels: no trip fee.
Nobody home: the trip fee only if the owner confirms it.
An empty rental's lockbox code fails: the tech waits 15 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee.
An area rug left at the plant after its free days: reminders; a storage fee only if the owner starts it, after written notice.
The truck-mounted unit is out: each job that needs it gets new times with no fee.
A storm warning: Sam closes the day, and every customer moves with no fee.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Pilot: started from the cleaner (service style). Carpet cleaning runs like house cleaning: a set service at the home, priced from the customer's answers, one visit in an arrival window. The cleaner's flow A (a rug drop-off) is already the carpet cleaner's less usual side, so its drop-off ops carry over.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Carpet Care (carpet cleaning, with upholstery cleaning as the second kind of work). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Rug Plant, Sam's second company, where area rugs are dropped off at the plant and picked up clean and dry.
Names: Jordan and Casey become carpet techs Kyle and Devon; Riley and Avery become rug techs Nico and Remy (Drew, Quinn and Reese are already master customers). The master's partner Jamie is Toni. Addresses: Alex at 31 Cedar Ave; Lee Carpet Care at 300 Mill Rd; Lee Rug Plant at 75 Dock St.
Every master number is kept: $179 carpet cleaning, 3 rooms; $150 for 2 rooms (the smallest job); $640 whole-home pet odor treatment from photos; a basement priced by the square foot at the visit ($245: basement $165, 20 stairs $80); $89 trip fee; $199 pet urine treatment for up to 3 rooms; found at the visit, $160 re-stretching and $95 rust stain. At the plant: $35 small rug, $40 runner, $20 fringe cleaning, $25 doormat, $55 rug cleaning with stain protector, $140 large wool rug, $90 pet stain treatment from photos, $25 inspection for a hand-knotted rug.
The old flowchart's $49 trip fee for a late cancel or nobody home became the master's $89 trip fee, so every fee, hold and refund still adds up. It's the example business's own price, held at booking (the old check file's fix E13: today's starting answer holds the trip fee).
Money paths, flow B: list|hold|bill is the main story (the trip fee held, the bill texted at DONE). Also used: list|none|bill (the old flowchart's pay link with nothing up front), list|card|card (a card saved and charged at DONE), list|none|own (paid at the door on the tech's own reader, cash or check: old nodes cp24a and cp24c), photos|hold|bill (the whole-home pet odor job) and visit|hold|bill (a basement by the square foot). No deposits or full price by default; Sam can set them per service.
Money paths, flow A: list|none|counter is the main story (nothing taken; paid at the counter at pick-up). Also list|full|none (the $55 cleaning with protector, prepaid), photos|none|counter (a pet stain from photos) and visit|none|counter (a hand-knotted rug priced at the counter). The plant's $20 fee only applies where Sam saves a card, which these paths don't use.
Priced by the room or the square foot: a room is up to 250 sq ft and a bigger one counts as 2 (B4-05, B4-07 more lines). Stains are noted before work: B8-18's words (UV light, measuring, photos, what may not come out said first). The own split B8-x01 to B8-x03 checks each room's size before work: as said; or a bigger room, which Alex OKs, skips, or cancels at the door with no trip fee (the old flowchart's firm price at the door, cp20 and cp21). Flow A does the same at intake (A8-23's words).
Carpet cleaning is never sent now: a fresh spill gets the soonest window, and a flood goes to a water-damage company. So S2-30, B4-81, B4-16, B6-03, B7-55 and B8-58 turn off their sent-now branches.
Danger words: flooding, a soaked carpet or pad, sewage, water near outlets (no booking: the safety steps, then a water-damage company), mold (that room is left out; the rest can be booked; Rosa's call B3-11 to B3-25), fleas or bedbugs (pest control first). Found at the visit, a wet pad or mold stops that room (B8-30's more lines).
Nobody home is allowed only for an empty home, like Kim's rental between tenants, with a lockbox (B8-69 and B8-70 keep both branches; the rename turns the gate code into a lockbox). Otherwise an adult is home for the visit (B8-67 keeps 'An adult must be there').
Kim's rental is the master's yard drain: the empty home with nobody there, the two-tech job (B7-53), the truck-mounted unit out for repair (B7-45) and the lockbox that fails (B8-52, B8-53). Weather doesn't stop indoor carpet work, so B7-05's 'Weather stops the job' is off; a storm warning closes the day (B7-23), as in the old flowchart.
The master's faucet sent to the shop is an area rug the tech takes from the home to Lee Rug Plant (B8-72 keeps both branches; B10-20, B10-27, B10-28 for a rug not taken back). The rented drying fan (B10-21) is an air mover left to dry the basement; B5-26's booked-ahead damage hold is off.
The warranty is the plug-in's 7-day re-treat promise: a spot that comes back gets a free re-treat (B10-08, B10-01's receipt line). The old flowchart's drying tips are B10-22's aftercare tips. The yearly plan is the master's: the same 3 rooms every 12 months at $150 a visit.
Upholstery is the second kind of work (loveseat $149, sofa $189, a sectional by free estimate visit), so S1-39 keeps its words; the sofa's fabric tag (W, S, W/S, X) is asked before times and decides how it's cleaned (B8-31: a sofa tagged S is cleaned dry).
Licenses: carpet, upholstery and rug cleaning need no state license where Sam works; S1-60, S1-63 and S2-28 take the registration-only branches, as for the cleaner.
